meaning:
δουλόω, -ῶ
(δοῦλος), [in LXX for עָבַד ;]
to enslave, bring into bondage: Act.7:6 (LXX), 2Pe.2:19; metaphorically, 1Co.9:19; pass., before ἐν, 1Co.7:15; τ. θεῷ, Rom.6:22; τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Rom.6:18; οἴνῳ, Tit.2:3; ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τ. κόσμου, Gal.4:3 (Cremer, 217).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: God spoke in this way: that his offspring would live as aliens in a strange land, and that they would be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
Being made free from sin, you became bondservants of righteousness.
Yet if the unbeliever departs, let there be separation. The brother or the sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God has called us in peace.
So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the elemental principles of the world.
and that older women likewise be reverent in behavior, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good,
promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him.
